data.name: The Whole Wreck
data.description: Staff walk-through of the Skyglass event. The salvager explains every piece in order, hands over the real items, and offers each boss as players face it, or a way to move on. Nothing is required.
data.successDescription: You walked the whole wreck, start to finish.

objectives.description:
The salvager sits by her fire on the shore of 210, a rolled chart across her knees.

"So you want the whole wreck, start to finish. Every Friday at 6 PM Central, a new hull surfaces and Wreck Sighted goes up on the Wake Island board. That quest is the kickoff: it sends people to the wreck, hands them this week's Watch Log and their first chart, and the wrecks stay open until Monday at 6 PM."
She holds out the chart. "A Tide Chart. It opens the Low Tide Run. Want to meet the crew it sends you into?"

nextObjectiveId.text: Show me the Low Tide crew

objectives.description:
She taps a page pinned under a stone by the fire.

"The Watch Log. Each page opens with a short story hook, then five challenges with their rewards, then the rules. There are two pages a week, one for levels 30 to 80 and one for 81 and up, and players pick theirs in Wreck Sighted. The pages hide on Wednesday, and Friday brings new ones. Nothing to do here, just know where they come from."

She drops a heavy sack at your feet. It clinks.

"Wreck Salvage. Players earn it in the wrecks and the chart runs, and spend it with me. I trade a deck chart for 4, a hold chart for 10, a sealed chart for 20, and the Lastlight Lantern for 30, once a week. My trades and my shore jobs come to people at random, on their daily NPC rolls, so nobody farms me dry. Here's 30, go try a trade."

She points at the two hulls on the reef, one grey with age, one glittering.

"Those are the Wrecks. The Faded Wreck is for 30 and up, the full Skyglass Wreck for 80 and up. Both are party dungeons for three, and both drop salvage and charts. The full Wreck is five decks: Deck Wardens and a Seal Charge, the Sentinel and the First Blade, the Oathkeeper and the Wayfinder, the Core Horror, then the Captain and his Sealwright. They're tuned for three, so going in alone, expect to lose."

"The last deck comes in two waves: three Deck Wardens first, then the Captain and the Sealwright."

The Captain steps down from the helm, and the Sealwright walks at his side.

"There he is. This is the fight the whole Wreck builds to."

objectives.description:
Back at the fire, she fans out six charts like a hand of cards.

"Charts are the solo side. Each one opens a Battle Pyramid run and is spent when the run starts. HP carries from fight to fight, a loss ends the run, and runs pay salvage and better charts back. Every run plays a little differently: terms you bargain for, the riddle door, the push-your-luck Haul, the run backwards, and the tainted route once a chart is steeped in Core Rot. Here's one of each deep chart, so you can play them later."

She nods down the beach, where the tide runs out farther than it should.

"The Driftline. That's the 30 to 80 band's own story: its own runs and its own bosses, so newer players have a road of their own. At the end of it waits the Driftline Captain."
The Driftline Captain takes the helm of the broken stern.

objectives.description:
She hands you a chart that smells of pitch and wet timber.

"The Hullbound Mender. His hold shrinks while you fight: he lays hull tiles, drops planks and splits the keel, and the walls keep coming in. His chart only drops in the Wreck, it's never sold. That's the Chart of the Closing Hold."
The Hullbound Mender sets down his mallet and picks up another.

objectives.description:
She sets a small lantern in your hands. Its light does not flicker in the wind.

"The Lastlight Lantern. It opens Crownhold, the climb up the mountain: rites, allies and alarms, decided by how you climb. Players get the Lantern from my weekly trade or, rarely, from the Wreck. At the top sits the Crowned Captain."
The Crowned Captain turns from the window, his Command Crown pale as frost.

objectives.description:
She lays four shards on a cloth, and they ring faintly against each other.

"The four shards. Keel from the Wreck and the Mender's hold, Crown from Crownhold, Tide from the Epic chart runs, Ledger from the Haul. Together they open the Mother of Echoes: three acts, one continuous fight, HP carried from act to act, and losing any act ends it."
Act one. The Mother Glass is singing.

objectives.description:
The glass throws you back onto the sand.

"In a real run, that's the end of it. Here, we just keep walking."

The fire has burned low. Out on the reef, the glass is already growing back.

"That's the whole wreck. Every week the glass grows back and a new hull surfaces on Friday, with a new page of the story. Everything I gave you is real, so play the full runs whenever you like."
You walked the whole wreck, start to finish.
